title: Research: a lower-frame obstruction for eight R439 phase-B blocks
body:
PR1062 shortens the ten R439 phase-B blocks while leaving their paid profile unchanged. This package proves that eight of those blocks cannot lower their frame bill by arbitrary exact resynthesis on their original wires with nested operation frames contained in the original rank-four block frame. Output dependencies force every wire to reach that frame; concavity shows that splitting the existing climb cannot improve the moment for 0 < a < 1.

The two remaining blocks have exceptional sources 19 and 22. Their broader lower-frame question stays open; exact inverse-matrix calculations exclude the simple source-star-prefix escape for both. Same-frame resynthesis preserves the itinerary on all ten blocks. This is a scoped structural result, with no new kappa, supplier adoption, or unrestricted circuit-optimality claim.

The independent standard-library checker imports no predecessor implementation. It checks rational span witnesses, exact binary maps, all 661 ordered frame paths, nine COPY charges, and all arbitrary dirty columns in both orientations on PR589, PR967 and both PR1062 words. Only research/r439-bblock-frame-barrier/ is added, based on current main bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f.

Validation:
- Python 3.12.14 registered replay passes: `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-bblock-frame-barrier`.
- All 13 focused tests pass, including integer Gram witnesses, semantic failures, missing-prefix-donor controls, and a constructive example showing why the full-span premise is necessary.
- Python 3.14.6 isolated optimized verification matches the complete certificate; selected-source baseline passes.
- 19 research-workflow tests pass with one Windows skip for the unchanged Unix timeout helper; local fixture settings are recorded in TASK.json.
- Final overlap refresh covers all 837 open PRs including drafts, with exact nearby heads. Discussion coverage is manual and partial; the connector exposes no Discussion mutation tool, so the claim is local.

Native/hosted replay, replacement bit-interface adoption, all-size realization, precision/tape, analytic transfer and proof-assistant formalization remain unrun. The selected construction is unchanged. README and TASK.json contain concrete next questions for the two exceptions and larger seams.

Credit Aaron Wang (PR1015), Ross Richardson (PR923), Sagar Thakrar (PR1062), Sricharan Vagvala (PR967), Gareth Davidson (PR915/926), DreamingOfClouds (PR589), eumemic (PR555/543), and the frame-optimum/checker lineage. Prepared by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review. Apache-2.0.
